pairs.question: Plane si ipsa die kalendarum quis stipulationem interponat, quid sequemur?
pairs.answer: Puto actum videri de sequentibus kalendis.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question and answer closing the section. Question kept whole including the 'si ipsa die kalendarum quis stipulationem interponat' setup so 'quid sequemur' has a referent; first word capitalized. Answer: dropped the connective 'et' and capitalized 'Puto'; the sentence runs to the end of the section, so no trailing cut.

pairs.question: Quid ergo si ipse, qui arbitrari debuit, moram fecerit?
pairs.answer: Magis probandum est a persona non esse recedendum eius, cuius arbitrium insertum est.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question (contrasting the case where the stipulator delayed) answered immediately. 'ipse, qui arbitrari debuit' is self-identifying so no extra setup needed; first word capitalized. Answer is the full following sentence to its full stop, the end of the section; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Stipulatus sum damam aut erotem servum dari: cum damam dares, ego quo minus acciperem, in mora fui: mortuus est dama: an putes me ex stipulatu actionem habere?
pairs.answer: Secundum massurii sabini opinionem puto te ex stipulatu agere non posse.
pairs.derivation: Epistolary consultation: the entire letter (the verbatim factual setup plus the closing 'an putes me ex stipulatu actionem habere?') is kept as the question so 'me' and the mora-scenario are intelligible; already ends with '?'. Answer: dropped the speech tag 'respondit:'; kept the operative first sentence to its full stop (the colon before 'nam is recte existimabat...', which is explanatory elaboration), capitalized 'Secundum' and supplied a terminal period. Proper names left lowercase as in source (normalization permits only first-word capitalization).
